question: Which of the three segments—SME, LAM and KAM—has the biggest and lowest percentage increases in consumption paid in EUR between 2012 and 2013?
final_sql: WITH cons AS ( SELECT c.Segment, SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date, 1, 4) = '2012' THEN y.Consumption ELSE 0 END) AS cons_2012, SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date, 1, 4) = '2013' THEN y.Consumption ELSE 0 END) AS cons_2013 FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c ON y.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE c.Currency = 'EUR' AND c.Segment IN ('SME', 'LAM', 'KAM') AND substr(y.Date, 1, 4) IN ('2012', '2013') GROUP BY c.Segment ), pct AS ( SELECT Segment, (cons_2013 - cons_2012) * 100.0 / cons_2013 AS pct_increase FROM cons ) SELECT 'biggest' AS which_segment, Segment FROM ( SELECT Segment FROM pct ORDER BY pct_increase DESC LIMIT 1 ) UNION ALL SELECT 'lowest' AS which_segment, Segment FROM ( SELECT Segment FROM pct ORDER BY pct_increase ASC LIMIT 1 );

question: How old was the patient who had the highest hemoglobin count at the time of the examination, and what is the doctor's diagnosis?
final_sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', E.[Examination Date]) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', P.Birthday) AS INTEGER) AS age, E.Diagnosis FROM Examination AS E INNER JOIN Patient AS P ON E.ID = P.ID INNER JOIN Laboratory AS L ON E.ID = L.ID AND E.[Examination Date] = L.Date ORDER BY L.HGB DESC LIMIT 1

       CAST(strftime('%Y','now') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', P.Birthday) AS INTEGER) AS age
FROM Patient AS P
JOIN Laboratory AS L
  ON P.ID = L.ID
WHERE L.HCT >= 52
GROUP BY P.ID, P.Birthday
HAVING COUNT(L.ID) > 2

question: How much higher in percentage is Ariel Borysiuk's overall rating than that of Paulin Puel?
final_sql: SELECT ((a.overall_rating - b.overall_rating) * 100.0 / b.overall_rating) AS percentage_higher FROM (SELECT pa.overall_rating FROM Player AS p JOIN Player_Attributes AS pa ON p.player_api_id = pa.player_api_id WHERE p.player_name = 'Ariel Borysiuk' ORDER BY pa.date DESC LIMIT 1) AS a CROSS JOIN (SELECT pa.overall_rating FROM Player AS p JOIN Player_Attributes AS pa ON p.player_api_id = pa.player_api_id WHERE p.player_name = 'Paulin Puel' ORDER BY pa.date DESC LIMIT 1) AS b;

rows: In a way, the measurement you proposed is widely used in case of error (model quality) analysis -- then it is called MAE, "mean absolute error".
If you would taste R, it is highly probable that you will resign from MATLAB (as in my case).
I think this is the first candidate to be moved to Stack Overflow.
@Sharpie, @Shane IMO to this extent it is a question about tools, so it is acceptable.
@Sharpie It is not only in contex of R -- to this end I've made a separate meta discussion for that, http://meta.stats.stackexchange.com/questions/35/how-much-programming-here
You should use Colin's answer, still your idea of making Monte Carlo simulation is also correct.
But still, using log changes the model -- for linear regression it is y~a*x+b, fo linear regression on log it is y~y0*exp(x/x0).
Right; it is just one variant among others.

What I wrote in my post is just that for a certain type of data/process/system there is only one *true* entropy definition. Sample Entropy is *not* an entropy measure, it is just some statistic with a confusing name. Make a question where you define the data for which you want to calculate the entropy, and will get the formula.
I think it does; still I'll try to extend the answer.

I agree, but I was indeed worried about the k parameter -- if the unbalance will create some class-wise differences in the observation densities in the feature space, the same k will tend to a smaller sphere in feature space for an observation from denser class. Won't it influence the k parameter optimization then?
No ;-) This was only to revive the pool.
Look at http://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/173/time-series-for-count-data-with-counts-20/ . It's not a duplicate, but the problem is similar at a first sight.
Here is my favorite paper about the topic: http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.13.7133&rep=rep1&type=pdf
Aptamer active motif selection, forest ground humidity forecasting, digit OCR, multispectral satellite image analysis, musical information retrieval, chemometry...

Regarding your question about energy, it's going to be difficult to answer. Do you know anything about your device? Do you know anything of the relationship between wind speed/direction and power? Do you know anything about the layout of the turbines at this particular site since that has a huge impact on the power as you no doubt are aware.

note that 'lag' is a term used mainly in analysis of data in time, referring to one thing occurring after another. This isn't a lag - it's perhaps more accurately called a shift - or maybe an offset - but shift is probably more common for distributions, they shift and scale.
i tried ploting it with out zero's but still there is a lag
well yes mainly from literature and other works on wind for the purpose of wind farms

I see that there is a bunch up near zero, do you have zero values in your data? In that case you will need to model zero values separately. So first suggestion would be to try Weibull for non zero values. Also why Weibull, is there particular reason, some reference from similar work perhaps?

question: What is the percentage of Story Spotlight cards that do not have a text box? List them by their ID.
final_sql: WITH stats AS (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards) AS percentage FROM cards WHERE isStorySpotlight = 1 AND isTextless = 0) SELECT c.id, stats.percentage FROM cards AS c CROSS JOIN stats WHERE c.isStorySpotlight = 1 AND c.isTextless = 0 ORDER BY c.id;

question: Is the set of cards with Adarkar Valkyrie only available outside the United States?
final_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 AND MIN(s.isForeignOnly) = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS isForeignOnly FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN sets AS s ON c.setCode = s.code WHERE c.name = 'Adarkar Valkyrie'
